body:
The root cause for this issue if the expire strategy of the DefaultDnsCache. The DefaultDnsCache controls the expiry per record, and remove the record from the list if the record is expired. In this case, the ipv4 record ttl is 60, while the ipv6 record ttl is 21599. 

So, ipv4 record will surely be expired before ipv6 record. And ipv6 record is still recorded in DefaulDnsCache, so query the DefaultDnsCache can still get the record for the URL with the ipv6 record.  

But as mentioned above, we are expecting the ipv4 record.

I am not sure what is the strategy used by InetAddress, but the Java resolver does always prefer ipv4 address every resolving.
@jianyuanzh hmm I think what you describe is actually what I would expect. Can you show me how exactly your build the `DnsNameResolver` ?

@normanmaurer , here is my demo script to check the TTL for DNS record:
```
String dns = "mirrors.servercentral.com.";

EventLoopGroup loopGroup = new NioEventLoopGroup(1)

StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder()
DnsNameResolver resolver = new DnsNameResolverBuilder(loopGroup.next())
        .channelType(NioDatagramChannel.class)
        .resolvedAddressTypes(ResolvedAddressTypes.IPV4_PREFERRED)
        .maxQueriesPerResolve(16)
        .resolveCache(new MyDefaultDnsCache(sb))
        .queryTimeoutMillis(500).build()


for (int i = 0; i < 10 ; i++) {
    Thread.sleep(60000)
    println resolver.resolveAll(dns).get()
}

println sb.toString()
loopGroup.shutdownGracefully()

class MyDefaultDnsCache extends DefaultDnsCache {
    final StringBuilder sb
    MyDefaultDnsCache(StringBuilder sb) {
        this.sb = sb;
    }
    @Override
    DnsCacheEntry cache(String hostname, DnsRecord[] additionals, InetAddress address, long originalTtl, EventLoop loop) {
        sb.append("originalTtl: ").append(address.getHostAddress()).append(" ").append(originalTtl).append("\n");
        return super.cache(hostname, additionals, address, originalTtl, loop)
    }
}
```

And by change the resolve type, I can sse that the TTL for ipv4 and ipv6 record differ greatlly.

@jianyuanzh so you say you think its a bug because it should try to refetch ipv4 as there was an ipv4 record before that was in the cache ?

yes, almost there.

As the DefaultDnsCache's impl, when ipv4 expired it will remove the ipv4 recod, and ipv6 is still there. The following dns reolving will always returning an IPv6 record.

issue.title: DefaultDnsCache should expire all records per hostname when one TTL i…

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
…s reached.

Motivation:

At the moment DefaultDnsCache will expire each record dependong on its own TTL. This may result in unexpected results for the end-user especially if the user for example uses IPV4_PREFERED but the cached AAAA records has a higher TTL then the A records and so the A record was removed. In this case we would only return the AAAA record and not even try to refresh.

Modifications:

Always expire all records for a hostname when one TTL is reached.

Result:

Fixes [#7329]
